newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone army rulers ask main banks to reopen.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone army rulers ask main banks to reopen.

text.p: Sierra Leone's army rulers have urged its two main commercial banks to reopen after hundreds of customers stormed the central bank demanding money from their accounts, state radio said on Friday.
The junta, again via state radio, told rice traders to cut the price of the staple or face unspecified drastic action.
State radio said the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council secretariat had asked Barclays and Standard Chartered Banks to reopen for business "because it involves the lives of people".

The two banks are West African nation's oldest surviving commercial banks and share about 80 percent of the market, financial sources say. They serve hundreds of thousands of public and private sector workers across the country.

Angry depositors, starved of funds in the chaos that followed a May 25 coup that ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, stormed the central bank on Thursday demanding their money, witnesses said.

Sierra Leone Labour Congress Secretary General Kandeh Yillah told reporters that the parent companies of the two banks had said they would remain shut "until the security situation in the the country improves considerably".
State-owned Sierra Leone Commercial Bank reopened on July 2.
Prices of basic foodstuffs such as rice have soared since the coup and a blockade by Sierra Leone's West African neighbours to persuade the junta to restore Kabbah.
A bag of rice has risen from 22,000 leones ($27) to 40,0000. The junta recommended a price of 22,000 and 25,000 leones.
